title: Omar's Day
paragraphs: Omar is a nurse. He lives in a small flat near the hospital. Every day he wakes up at six o'clock.
He drinks tea and eats bread with cheese for breakfast. Then he walks to work. He likes his job because he helps people.
In the evening, Omar calls his mother. On Fridays, he visits his family and they eat lunch together.

When does he visit his family?
questions.explanationAr: On Fridays, he visits his family.

title: A Trip to Petra
paragraphs: Last spring, Lina and her brother travelled to Petra. They left Amman early in the morning and arrived after three hours.
The weather was warm and sunny. They walked through the narrow canyon and suddenly saw the Treasury. Lina couldn't believe how beautiful it was.
They climbed many steps to see the Monastery. It was tiring, but the view from the top was amazing. In the evening, they ate dinner at a local restaurant and talked about their favourite moments.

title: The Interview
paragraphs: Sara had been looking for a job for months when she finally received an invitation for an interview at a large tech company. She was excited but also very nervous.
The night before, she researched the company and practised answering common questions with her friend. She decided to wear a simple, professional outfit.

During the interview, the manager asked her about a time she had solved a difficult problem. Sara explained how she had organised a project with a tight deadline. A week later, she received an email: she had got the job.

questions.prompt: How did Sara feel before the interview?
questions.explanationAr: She was excited but also very nervous.

questions.prompt: What did she do the night before?
questions.explanationAr: She researched the company and practised.

title: The Rise of Remote Work
paragraphs: Over the past few years, remote work has shifted from a rare privilege to a widespread practice. Many companies discovered that employees could remain productive without commuting to an office every day.
However, the change has not been without challenges. Some workers report feeling isolated, while managers struggle to maintain team spirit and clear communication across different time zones.
As a result, a hybrid model is emerging as a compromise. Employees spend part of the week at home and part in the office, combining flexibility with the benefits of face-to-face collaboration.

title: Learning in the Age of AI
paragraphs: Artificial intelligence is reshaping the way people acquire new skills. Personalised tutors can now adapt explanations to a learner's level, provide instant feedback, and generate endless practice material.

Critics, nevertheless, caution against over-reliance on such tools. They argue that genuine mastery requires sustained effort, and that the struggle to recall information is precisely what consolidates it in long-term memory.
The most promising approach, therefore, may be one that leverages technology to remove unnecessary friction while preserving the productive difficulty that makes learning stick.
